items.name: Nvidia Blackwell-class AI GPUs
items.what_it_is: Nvidia's newest and fastest AI training chips, the industry standard for building frontier AI models.
items.used_for: Training and running the largest AI models.
items.status_detail: Top-end Blackwell chips cannot be sold to China. Reports say the White House refused a cut-down Blackwell variant (B30A) for China; the date of that report is unconfirmed, so treat as likely but not certain.
items.evidence: Reported B30A would run at roughly half the speed of Nvidia's B300; talks with the administration were public in Aug 2025.

items.name: Nvidia H200 (licensed sales)
items.what_it_is: The previous-generation Nvidia Hopper AI chip, still far more powerful than the downgraded chips China was allowed before.
items.used_for: Training large AI models.
items.status_detail: US approved case-by-case licenses in Dec 2025/Jan 2026 (25% of revenue to the US government; China volume capped relative to US sales; independent testing). Beijing first blocked imports at customs, then by Aug 2026 reportedly allowed small batches (about 10,000 each to ByteDance and Tencent), with NDRC approval needed and use steered to training. No Sept-Oct 2026 update found.
items.evidence: US clearance allows up to 100,000 H200s per Chinese buyer; Nvidia reportedly holds about 500,000 H200s in inventory.
items.contested_note: Supporters say selling older chips keeps China hooked on US tech and funds the US government; critics say it hands China frontier-class training compute and Beijing is using it selectively to build domestic chips.

items.tip: Powerful older Nvidia AI chips the US licenses to China, though Beijing has allowed only small batches.

items.name: Nvidia H20 (China-specific chip)
items.what_it_is: A deliberately slowed-down Nvidia AI chip designed to meet US export limits for China.
items.used_for: Running (inference) and smaller-scale training of AI models.
items.status_detail: Banned in April 2025, then licensed again in Aug 2025 with a 15% revenue share to the US. Nvidia reportedly wound down H20 production and inventory is limited; H200 has largely superseded it. Current 2026 volumes not confirmed.
items.evidence: Nvidia agreed to give the US government 15% of H20 China revenue.
items.contested_note: Critics argue the 15% revenue-share deal turns export controls into a fee and may be unconstitutional as an export tax; supporters call it a pragmatic compromise.

items.tip: A deliberately slowed Nvidia chip made for China, now largely replaced by the H200.

items.name: AMD MI308 AI GPUs
items.what_it_is: AMD's cut-down version of its MI300 AI chip made for the China market.
items.used_for: AI model training and inference in data centers.
items.status_detail: Needed a license from April 2025 (AMD took an $800M charge); license applications proceeded from July 2025 and AMD said in Dec 2025 it was authorized to ship certain MI308 chips, paying a 15% fee. A more powerful China chip, MI309, reportedly failed the license test. No 2026 shipment data found.
items.evidence: AMD booked about $800 million in charges when the license requirement hit in April 2025.

items.name: Chip design software (EDA)
items.what_it_is: The specialized software engineers use to design and test computer chips; three firms (Synopsys, Cadence, Siemens EDA) dominate it.
items.used_for: Designing every advanced chip, including Chinese AI chips.
items.status_detail: The US imposed license requirements on EDA sales to China in May 2025, then rescinded them in July 2025 as part of a deal tied to China's rare earth export concessions. No evidence found of reimposition, but the 2026 situation was not directly confirmed.
items.evidence: Synopsys said the May 29, 2025 restriction letter was rescinded effective immediately.
items.contested_note: Critics say lifting EDA curbs traded away a key chokepoint for rare earths; the administration framed it as a reciprocal deal.

sources.title: White House lifts chip design export ban on China in exchange for rare earth compromise (Tom's Hardware)

items.chokepoint_note: Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens together hold an estimated 70–85% of chip design software, depending on how the market is counted.
items.tip: Software used to design every advanced chip; US limits on China were imposed in May 2025, then lifted.

items.name: Etch and deposition tools (Applied Materials, Lam)
items.what_it_is: Machines that lay down and carve away ultra-thin layers on silicon wafers to build chips.
items.used_for: Manufacturing advanced logic and memory chips, including Huawei's AI chips.
items.status_detail: Advanced-node tools need licenses and Entity List firms (SMIC, Huawei fabs) are largely cut off, while mature-node sales continue. The Sept 2025 Affiliates Rule extended limits to 50%-owned subsidiaries; reportedly suspended until Nov 9, 2026 unless extended. Applied paid a record $252M BIS settlement in Feb 2026 over ion implanters shipped to SMIC via South Korea. Lam (Fremont) is the other major supplier; China is a large share of both firms' revenue.
items.evidence: Applied expected the Affiliates Rule to cut about $600M from fiscal 2026 sales.
items.contested_note: Industry argues restrictions hand share to Japanese and Chinese toolmakers; hawks say gaps still let China build advanced chips.

sources.title: BIS 2026 enforcement agenda takes shape (Mondaq)
Applied Materials fined $252M for ignoring export curbs (Bits&Chips)
US Chip Export Controls Timeline (Referently)

items.tip: US machines that build chips are largely cut off for Chinese advanced fabs; older-node sales continue.

items.name: Inspection and metrology tools (KLA)
items.what_it_is: Machines that scan wafers for microscopic defects so fabs can fix problems and raise yield.
items.used_for: Making advanced chips at usable yields; KLA has near-monopoly share in many inspection steps.
items.status_detail: Same licensing regime as other US tools; YMTC and other Entity List firms cut off from advanced tools since Dec 2022. One unverified report claims new BIS tool rules in April 2026 hit KLA shares; not confirmed from a primary source.
items.evidence: KLA shares reportedly fell 4.2% on April 16, 2026 after export-control news (unverified promotional source).

items.tip: KLA machines find wafer defects; Entity List firms are cut off from advanced tools under US licensing.

items.name: Servicing, spare parts and software updates for fab tools
items.what_it_is: The engineers, replacement parts and software patches that keep already-installed US machines running in Chinese fabs.
items.used_for: Keeping existing Chinese chip production lines running.
items.status_detail: US-person support for advanced fabs requires a license since Oct 2022. BIS removed Samsung and SK hynix China fabs from the VEU program effective Dec 31, 2025, with annual licenses reportedly granted for 2026 (not confirmed from a primary source). BIS also penalizes in-China transfers to SMIC (e.g. Exyte, Jan 2026).
items.evidence: Applied Materials and others saw China service revenue pressured; Exyte paid $1.5M for in-China transfer to SMIC Beijing.

items.name: High-bandwidth memory (HBM)
items.what_it_is: Very fast stacked memory placed next to AI chips; AI accelerators need it to perform.
items.used_for: Pairing with AI GPUs for training and inference.
items.status_detail: Dec 2024 BIS rule restricts HBM exports to China; Micron says it has not sold HBM there. China's CXMT is reportedly aiming for HBM3 production by late 2026, so this leverage is eroding. Samsung (Korea) is the main supplier Chinese firms stocked up on before the ban.
items.evidence: Micron reportedly has sold no HBM to China since the Dec 2024 rule.

items.chokepoint_note: Only three companies make HBM: SK Hynix (~62%), Micron (~21%) and Samsung (~17%) by Q2 2025 shipments.

items.tip: Fast stacked memory that AI chips need; US rules limit sales to China and Micron says it sold none.

items.name: EUV lithography machines
items.what_it_is: The only machines in the world that print the finest circuit patterns on chips, made solely by ASML.
items.used_for: Making the most advanced AI chips (below roughly 5nm) at scale.
items.status_detail: No EUV machine has been shipped to China; Dutch and US controls bar it. Press coverage describes China as roughly a decade or more away from its own EUV tool.
items.evidence: ASML is the world's only EUV maker; UBS analysts put China's gap at at least a decade (as reported by Asiae/Bloomberg-derived coverage).

items.chokepoint_note: ASML is the only company in the world that makes EUV machines.
items.tip: Only ASML makes these machines; none has shipped to China, which is reportedly about a decade away.

items.name: ASML DUV immersion lithography and servicing
items.what_it_is: Older-generation chip printing machines that, used repeatedly, can still make fairly advanced chips.
items.used_for: Making 7nm-class chips for Huawei AI processors and most mature-node chips in China.
items.status_detail: The most advanced DUV immersion tools need Dutch licenses; older DUV tools still sell. The pending US MATCH Act (introduced April 2026, not passed as of Oct 2026) would extend controls to DUV and possibly servicing; the Dutch government opposes it.
items.evidence: China was 36% of ASML sales in 2024 and 33% in 2025 (its largest market); ASML guides to about 20% in 2026.
items.contested_note: ASML and the Dutch government argue broader curbs speed Chinese self-reliance and hurt allied firms; US hawks say they are needed to stop 7nm/5nm expansion.

items.tip: Older ASML printing machines can still make fairly advanced chips; the most advanced need Dutch licenses.

items.name: Etch, deposition and coating tools
items.what_it_is: Machines that carve and coat silicon wafers; Tokyo Electron is a world leader.
items.used_for: Fabricating logic and memory chips, including chips for AI hardware.
items.status_detail: Japan has controlled 23 categories of advanced chipmaking equipment since July 2023, with more items added in 2025. Most tool sales to non-listed Chinese customers still flow legally. The US MATCH Act proposal would pressure Japan to go further and may cover servicing.
items.evidence: China was 34.1% of Tokyo Electron revenue in the fiscal year ended March 2026, falling to 26.8% in the final quarter.
items.contested_note: Japanese firms say further curbs cost them sales without stopping Chinese progress.

items.tip: Japan controls 23 categories of chipmaking tools, but most sales to other Chinese customers still flow.

items.name: Photoresist and high-purity chemicals
items.what_it_is: Light-sensitive coatings and ultra-pure chemicals used to print patterns on wafers; Japanese firms dominate.
items.used_for: Every step of chip lithography, including advanced nodes.
items.status_detail: No formal Japanese ban confirmed. In Nov 2025 social media rumors said Japan had halted photoresist shipments to China amid the Takaichi dispute; no government or company confirmed it. Current 2026 status unverified.
items.evidence: Four Japanese firms held 72.5% of global photoresist in 2021; Chinese domestic substitution estimated below 5% (TrendForce). Shin-Etsu halted deliveries to China briefly in 2021.
items.contested_note: China says it can find domestic and foreign alternatives; Japanese firms deny a halt.

items.tip: Japanese firms dominate these chip-printing coatings; a reported shipment halt is rumor, not confirmed.

items.name: TSMC leading-edge chip manufacturing
items.what_it_is: The world's best contract chip factory; Chinese AI chip designers cannot match its quality.
items.used_for: Fabricating advanced AI accelerators.
items.status_detail: US foundry due-diligence rule (Jan 2025) requires fabs to vet customers for 16/14nm and below; TSMC stopped shipping 7nm-and-below AI chips to many Chinese designers. Taiwan also put Huawei and SMIC on its export blacklist. Current enforcement status not re-verified for late 2026.
items.evidence: TSMC made about $500 million of wafers for Sophgo that ended up in Huawei's Ascend 910B; a $1B+ US fine was reportedly considered.

items.name: Korean memory fabs inside China (VEU ended)
items.what_it_is: Samsung and SK Hynix run big memory factories in China (Xi'an, Wuxi, Dalian) that depend on imported US-origin tools.

In late Dec 2025 the US reportedly granted annual licenses for 2026 covering Xi'an, Wuxi and Dalian, limited to keeping existing operations running, no expansion or upgrades. 2027 license outcome not confirmed.
items.evidence: BIS estimated the change would generate over 1,000 additional license applications per year.

items.what_it_is: A way of stacking processor and memory chips together on one base; TSMC's version is the industry standard for AI chips.

items.status_detail: No CoWoS-specific rule confirmed; access is blocked in practice via the foundry rule and TSMC stopping advanced-node work for Chinese designers. Huawei reportedly uses a Chinese copy of CoWoS-S. Not verified for 2026.

items.used_for: Training and running large AI models in China
items.status_detail: CHARGED, NOT PROVEN. Super Micro co-founder Wally Liaw and Steven Chang were indicted in SDNY in March 2026 (export-control conspiracy, smuggling, defrauding the US). Liaw pleaded not guilty. Contractor Ting-Wei Sun pleaded guilty on Oct 8, 2026 (sentencing set Sept 2027). Super Micro itself is not charged and says it is cooperating. The Taiwan and Singapore transit legs come from reporting and the route listed here is approximate.
items.evidence: Prosecutors allege about $2.5B of servers (Nvidia B200, H100, H200) shipped since 2024; fake 'dummy' servers were allegedly staged to fool inspectors.

items.used_for: Chinese-owned subsidiaries buying advanced chips
items.status_detail: RULE GAP, NOT A CASE. BIS Affiliates Rule was suspended for one year from Nov 10, 2025 under the US-China trade deal. Federal Register text reinstates it Nov 10, 2026; a Sept 2026 truce extension to Jan 10, 2027 reportedly extends the suspension, but I found no BIS notice confirming it.
items.evidence: Suspension scheduled to end Nov 9, 2026 unless BIS extends it.
items.contested_note: Washington traded the suspension for China pausing its rare-earth licensing regime.

items.name: Stockpiling Samsung HBM before Dec 2024 rules
items.what_it_is: Chinese firms bought up high-bandwidth memory ahead of the US ban to build AI chips.
items.used_for: Huawei and other Chinese AI accelerators
items.status_detail: REPORTED. Reuters said Huawei, Baidu and others stockpiled Samsung HBM in 2024. A later estimate put purchases at about 7M chips (over $1B) in the month before the Dec 2024 restrictions. This was legal at the time.
items.evidence: China was about 30% of Samsung's HBM revenue in H1 2024.

sources.title: Taipei Times: Chinese firms stockpiling high-end Samsung chips

items.tip: Reported: Chinese firms bought up Samsung memory before the December 2024 ban, which was legal then.

items.name: Stockpiling chipmaking tools before Dutch/Japan curbs
items.what_it_is: China rushed to import chipmaking machines before new Dutch, Japanese and US limits took effect.
items.used_for: Building chip fabs
items.status_detail: REPORTED. Imports were nearly $5B in June-July 2023 (up 70%) and $25.9B in the first seven months of 2024 (up 44%). Legal at the time; it blunts the controls' later impact.
items.evidence: Chinese tool imports up 44% to $25.9B in Jan-Jul 2024.

sources.title: Mobile World Live: China chipmaking equipment imports soar
Tom's Hardware: China's chip imports boom as it stockpiles

items.tip: Reported: China rushed to import chipmaking machines before new limits, which blunts the controls.

items.name: Gallium

to.site: US defense and chip electronics hub, Northern Virginia

items.what_it_is: A soft metal used to make fast chips and radar parts.
items.used_for: Radar, 5G and power chips, LEDs, compound semiconductors.
items.status_detail: China banned gallium/germanium/antimony exports to the US in Dec 2024; the ban on US-bound shipments is suspended until 2026-11-27 after the Oct 2025 Trump-Xi meeting, but the metals stay on the licence list and military end users remain barred. Not confirmed whether it will be extended past Nov 27 2026.
items.evidence: USGS profile puts China at about 99% of primary gallium output in 2024.

items.name: Heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium)

to.site: Northern Virginia data center cluster, Ashburn

items.used_for: Magnets for cooling fans, hard drives, motors, defense systems.

projects.name: TSMC Arizona fabs
projects.what: Makes the most advanced logic chips, including AI accelerators, in the US.
projects.closes_gap: Advanced logic chips made only in Taiwan.
projects.status_detail: Fab 1 (4nm) has been in high-volume production since late 2024; Fab 2 construction is finished and tool installation starts in Q3 2026 for 3nm output around 2027 (per Nikkei via a secondary source). Dates and investment totals differ across sources.

projects.name: Intel Ohio fab
projects.what: Planned leading-edge chip factory to make Intel's own processors and contract chips.
projects.closes_gap: Advanced logic chip capacity outside Taiwan and Asia.
projects.status_detail: Intel's February 2025 memo, reported March 3, 2025, moved Fab 1 production to 2030 (from late 2026) and Fab 2 to 2031; construction continues at a slower pace. Hoodline's 2026 coverage repeats the 2030 date but cites the 2025 memo, so no newer date is confirmed.
